prompt: Two ProximityPrompts never appear in my game. (1) A vending machine: Workspace.VendingMachine is a Model with no PrimaryPart, and the prompt sits at VendingMachine > Folder 'Interact' > ProximityPrompt. (2) A lever: the prompt is a child of a Lever part that sits inside a closed glass display case (the glass is a separate part around it). Both prompts are Enabled and I am standing well inside MaxActivationDistance. Explain why each one fails and how to fix it.
answer_key: A ProximityPrompt only works when parented to a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model (with PrimaryPart set) in the Workspace; under a Folder (or a Model without PrimaryPart) it never shows, so move it under a part/attachment or set the model's PrimaryPart

RequiresLineOfSight is true by default and hides the prompt when the path from the camera to the prompt's parent is obstructed; the glass case blocks it (the prompt's own parent part/model is excluded from the check)
Lever fix: set RequiresLineOfSight = false, or move the prompt (e.g. on an Attachment/part) to a spot outside the case that the camera can see

responses.R1:
(1) A ProximityPrompt only shows when parented to a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model with a PrimaryPart (it needs a world position). A Folder inside a model with no PrimaryPart gives it no position, so it never appears. Fix: parent the prompt to a part (e.g. the machine's front panel) or to an Attachment in that part, or set VendingMachine.PrimaryPart and parent the prompt to the Model.
(2) RequiresLineOfSight defaults to true: the prompt raycasts from the camera to the prompt's position and any blocking part (the glass case) hides it. Fix: set RequiresLineOfSight = false, or move the prompt to a part/Attachment outside the glass, or make the glass non-blocking for the check (CanQuery = false, only possible with CanCollide = false). Also check MaxActivationDistance, Enabled, ProximityPromptService.Enabled and that the prompt is not under a descendant of a client-only stream-out region.
responses.R2:
(1) Vending machine: a ProximityPrompt only shows when its parent gives it a world position: a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model WITH a PrimaryPart. Its parent here is a Folder inside a Model that has no PrimaryPart, so the prompt has no position and never appears. Fix: parent the prompt to a part or an Attachment (for example a hidden anchored "PromptAnchor" part or an attachment on the front panel). Or set VendingMachine.PrimaryPart and parent the prompt to the Model directly, not to a Folder.
(2) Lever: RequiresLineOfSight defaults to true, so the engine raycasts from the camera to the prompt's position, and the glass case blocks that ray. Fix: set RequiresLineOfSight = false, or move the prompt to an Attachment outside the glass. Another option is to make the glass ignored by the check (CanQuery = false while CanCollide = false), but test that it no longer blocks.
responses.R3: (1) A ProximityPrompt only works when parented to a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model (a Model uses its PrimaryPart/pivot for position). Under a Folder it has no world position, so it never shows. Fix: move it into a part of the machine (or an Attachment on the button part), or parent it to the Model and set VendingMachine.PrimaryPart. (2) RequiresLineOfSight defaults to true: the engine raycasts from the camera to the prompt, and the glass case blocks that ray, so the prompt is suppressed. Fix: set RequiresLineOfSight = false on the lever prompt, or move the prompt to a part/attachment outside the glass (or make the glass non-queryable if nothing else needs to hit it).

Here the parent is a Folder inside a Model that has no PrimaryPart, so the prompt has no position and never shows. Fix: move the prompt under a part of the machine (or an Attachment in that part), or set VendingMachine.PrimaryPart and parent the prompt to the model. (2) RequiresLineOfSight defaults to true. The engine casts a ray from the camera to the prompt's parent, and the glass case blocks that ray, so the prompt is hidden. Fix: set RequiresLineOfSight = false, or put the prompt on an Attachment or part outside the glass. You could also set the glass's CanQuery = false so the line-of-sight check ignores it, but that hides the glass from all raycasts.

(1) Vending machine: a ProximityPrompt only shows when its parent gives it a world position: a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model that has a PrimaryPart. Here its parent is a Folder, and the Folder sits in a Model with no PrimaryPart, so the prompt has no position and never shows. Fix: parent the prompt to a part, or better to an Attachment inside the machine's front part (e.g. Machine.Front.PromptAttachment). Setting VendingMachine.PrimaryPart and parenting the prompt to the Model also works.
(2) Lever: RequiresLineOfSight defaults to true. The prompt raycasts from the camera to the lever, and the glass case blocks that ray, so the prompt is hidden. Its parent here is a Folder, and the Model above it has no PrimaryPart, so the prompt has no position and is never drawn. Fix: parent the prompt to an Attachment inside the front panel part, or to that part itself. Setting VendingMachine.PrimaryPart and parenting the prompt to the Model also works, but an Attachment lets you place it exactly.
(2) Lever: RequiresLineOfSight defaults to true, and the glass case is a separate part blocking the line of sight from the camera to the prompt. prompt: Overhead name tags are a BillboardGui in each character's Head with Size = UDim2.fromOffset(200, 50) and AlwaysOnTop = true. Players complain the tags show through walls, are visible from across the whole map, and stay the same pixel size no matter how far away the character is. The designer wants tags hidden behind walls, not drawn beyond about 100 studs, and shrinking with distance like a real object. Which BillboardGui properties should change, and why?
answer_key: AlwaysOnTop = true makes the billboard render on top of all 3D content (ignores occlusion); set it to false so walls hide the tag
MaxDistance defaults to 0/infinite, meaning no distance limit; set MaxDistance = 100 so it stops rendering beyond 100 studs
Offset size is a fixed pixel size; the scale components of a BillboardGui's Size are measured in studs, so use a scale size (e.g. UDim2.fromScale(4, 1)) to make the tag shrink with distance

responses.R1:
- AlwaysOnTop = false: the tag is depth-tested, so walls hide it. With true, it always renders over 3D geometry.
- MaxDistance = 100: the tag is not drawn when the camera is more than 100 studs from the adornee. The default is infinite (0/inf), which is why it shows across the whole map.
- Size in Scale (studs) instead of Offset (pixels), e.g. Size = UDim2.fromScale(4, 1). The scale components of a BillboardGui's Size are world studs, so the tag shrinks with distance like a real object. Offset is fixed screen pixels, which is why it never changes size. Use TextScaled (with a UITextSizeConstraint if needed) on the label so the text follows the frame.
- Optional: StudsOffset / StudsOffsetWorldSpace = Vector3.new(0, 2, 0) to lift it above the head. Set LightInfluence = 0 to keep it readable at night.
- Optional: DistanceLowerLimit / DistanceUpperLimit / DistanceStep only matter for offset-sized gui scaling. Scale sizing is the simple fix.

prompt: For a round-based game a server script sets Players.CharacterAutoLoads = false. Now players who join have no character, and players who die never respawn. I also set Players.RespawnTime = 3 but nothing changes. Explain what is happening and describe (or sketch) the minimal server-side fix.
answer_key: With CharacterAutoLoads = false the engine never spawns characters automatically (not on join, not after death); the server must call player:LoadCharacterAsync() itself
RespawnTime only applies when CharacterAutoLoads is true (default 5 seconds), so changing it has no effect here

Fix sketch: call LoadCharacterAsync from a server Script on PlayerAdded (or when the round starts) and after Humanoid.Died (hooked via CharacterAdded) once your own delay/round logic allows; it yields and replaces/removes the old character

responses.R1:
With CharacterAutoLoads = false the engine never spawns characters, neither on join nor after death. Your scripts own spawning completely. RespawnTime is only used by the automatic respawn, so it does nothing now. Minimal server fix: call LoadCharacterAsync yourself (LoadCharacter was renamed in Jan 2026; the old name still works).
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
Players.CharacterAutoLoads = false
local RESPAWN = 3
local function spawn(p) if p.Parent then p:LoadCharacterAsync() end end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(p)
  p.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char)
    char:WaitForChild("Humanoid").Died:Connect(function()
      task.wait(RESPAWN); spawn(p)
    end)
  end)
  spawn(p) -- or wait for the round to start
end)
```
Connect CharacterAdded before the first spawn. Only spawn from the server. In a round game, gate spawn() on the round state (e.g. put dead players in a spectator queue).
responses.R2:
With CharacterAutoLoads = false the engine never spawns characters: not on join and not on death. RespawnTime only applies to automatic respawns, so it does nothing now. You must call Player:LoadCharacterAsync() (old name LoadCharacter, renamed Jan 2026) yourself on the server:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
Players.CharacterAutoLoads = false
local RESPAWN = 3
local function spawn(p) if p.Parent then pcall(function() p:LoadCharacterAsync() end) end end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(p)
  p.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char)
    char:WaitForChild("Humanoid").Died:Connect(function()
      task.wait(RESPAWN); spawn(p) -- or wait until round logic allows
    end)
  end)
  spawn(p) -- or spawn when the round starts
end)
```
Connect CharacterAdded before the first load; call it from a server Script only.
responses.R3:
CharacterAutoLoads = false turns off all automatic spawning: no character on join and no respawn after death. RespawnTime only applies to the automatic respawn, so it does nothing now. You must spawn manually with Player:LoadCharacter() (or LoadCharacterAsync where available) on the server:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
Players.CharacterAutoLoads = false
local function onPlayer(p)
  p.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char)
    char:WaitForChild('Humanoid').Died:Connect(function()
      task.delay(3, function()
        if p.Parent then p:LoadCharacter() end
      end)
    end)
  end)
  p:LoadCharacter()
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayer)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayer, p) end
```
For rounds, call LoadCharacter when the round logic wants the player in instead of on death.

prompt: Glass panes in a lab have CanCollide = false and CanQuery = false so players can walk through them. A server-side laser uses workspace:Raycast(origin, direction, params) and is supposed to stop at the glass, but the ray passes straight through. The RaycastParams has no filter set. Why, and what is the fix?
answer_key: Spatial queries (Raycast, shapecasts, overlap queries) never include parts with CanQuery = false; CanQuery = false only takes effect because CanCollide is false, so the glass is invisible to the ray

Fix: set CanQuery = true on the glass while keeping CanCollide = false (and leave RaycastParams.RespectCanCollide false, since that would use CanCollide instead and skip the glass again), or add a separate query-only part

responses.R1: CanQuery = false removes a part from ALL spatial queries (raycasts, GetPartsInPart, etc.), regardless of RaycastParams filters, so the ray can never hit it. CanCollide = false alone is enough to let players walk through, and raycasts hit non-collidable parts by default (RespectCanCollide is false). Fix: set CanQuery = true on the glass (keep CanCollide = false). If you need finer control, use collision groups for walk-through and a RaycastParams filter / CollisionGroup on the ray, e.g. exclude player characters.
responses.R2: Raycasts ignore parts whose CanQuery is false (CanQuery only takes effect when CanCollide is false, which is the case here). Filters cannot bring them back. Fix: set CanQuery = true on the glass (keep CanCollide = false so players walk through). If other queries should ignore the glass, exclude it there via their params (FilterDescendantsInstances/ExcludeInstances) or a collision group; for the laser you can use a dedicated CollisionGroup on RaycastParams, or RespectCanCollide=false (default) so the non-colliding but queryable glass is hit.
responses.R3: CanQuery = false removes a part from all spatial queries: Raycast, Blockcast, Shapecast and the GetPartsIn* overlap queries. The ray cannot hit the glass whatever the filter says. CanQuery can only be turned off when CanCollide is also false, which is exactly this setup. Fix: set CanQuery = true on the glass and keep CanCollide = false so players still walk through. The laser then hits it (RaycastParams.RespectCanCollide defaults to false, so non-collidable parts are still hit). If other queries must ignore the glass, filter it out per query with RaycastParams/OverlapParams (an exclude list or a CollisionGroup) instead of turning off CanQuery.
responses.R4:
CanQuery = false removes a part from all spatial queries: raycasts, shapecasts and GetPartsInPart / GetPartBoundsInBox. The RaycastParams filter can't bring it back. (CanQuery is only honoured when CanCollide is false, which is the case here.) So the laser can't see the glass.
Fix: set CanQuery = true on the glass and keep CanCollide = false. Players still walk through it, and raycasts hit it again (RespectCanCollide defaults to false, so non-colliding parts are still hit). If other rays (guns, camera) should ignore the glass, filter it per query instead: put the glass in a "Glass" collision group, or add it to those rays' ExcludeInstances / FilterDescendantsInstances. The laser's params leave it in.
responses.R5:
CanQuery = false takes a part out of every spatial query: Raycast, shapecasts, GetPartsInPart and so on. The ray therefore never sees the glass, no matter what RaycastParams contain. (CanQuery can only be turned off when CanCollide is false, which is your setup.) Your filter isn't the problem.
Fix: set the glass to CanQuery = true and keep CanCollide = false. Players still walk through, because CanCollide is what blocks movement, and the laser ray now hits the glass. If other raycasts (guns, camera) must ignore the glass, exclude it in their params (ExcludeInstances / FilterDescendantsInstances), or tag it and filter on the hit. Note that RaycastParams.RespectCanCollide is false by default, so non-colliding parts are hit as long as CanQuery is true.
responses.R6:
Raycasts skip any part with CanQuery = false. That is the whole purpose of CanQuery (it only takes effect when CanCollide is false, which is true here). So the glass does not exist to the laser, and no filter can bring it back. Fixes:
- Set glass CanQuery = true and keep CanCollide = false. Players can still walk through it, and rays now hit it. Then filter out other unwanted parts with RaycastParams (ExcludeInstances/IncludeInstances, or the older FilterDescendantsInstances + FilterType).
- Or put players and glass in collision groups that don't collide, keep the glass CanCollide = true and CanQuery = true, and give the laser's RaycastParams.CollisionGroup a group that collides with glass.

grader_notes: Item 2: the RespectCanCollide remark is not required for full credit; setting CanQuery = true (or an equivalent query-only part) is enough.

prompt:
A server script spawns enemies:
```lua
local template = game.ReplicatedStorage.Enemies.Goblin
local function spawnGoblin(cf)
    local g = template:Clone()
    g:PivotTo(cf)
    g.Parent = workspace
end
```
It errors with "attempt to index nil with 'PivotTo'". We found that an editor plugin had set Archivable = false on Goblin. A teammate then tried to avoid cloning by parenting the template itself to workspace, calling template:Destroy() when the goblin dies, and parenting it again for the next spawn; that throws "The Parent property of Goblin is locked". Explain both errors and the correct pattern.
answer_key: Clone() returns nil when called directly on an instance whose Archivable is false (non-Archivable descendants are also skipped when an ancestor is cloned); set Archivable = true on the template
Destroy() sets Parent to nil and locks the Parent property (and disconnects connections and destroys descendants), so a destroyed instance can never be reparented or reused
Correct pattern: leave the template untouched in storage, Clone a fresh copy for every spawn, Destroy only the clone when it dies, and drop references to destroyed instances

responses.R1:
Error 1: Instance:Clone() returns nil when the instance's Archivable is false, and it also skips non-Archivable descendants. g is nil, so g:PivotTo errors. Fix: set Goblin.Archivable = true (and check descendants). Keep the template in ServerStorage, since the server spawns them.
Error 2: Destroy() sets Parent to nil, locks the Parent property, and disconnects connections. A destroyed instance can never be parented again, which is why you get "Parent property ... is locked". Never Destroy a template you plan to reuse.
Correct pattern: clone per spawn and destroy the clone.
```lua
local template = game.ServerStorage.Enemies.Goblin -- Archivable = true
local function spawnGoblin(cf)
    local g = template:Clone()
    assert(g, "Goblin not archivable")
    g:PivotTo(cf)
    g.Parent = workspace
    g.Humanoid.Died:Once(function()
        task.delay(3, function() g:Destroy() end)
    end)
    return g
end
```
If clone cost matters, pool: reset instances and park them (Parent = nil or a storage folder) instead of destroying them.
responses.R2: Error 1: Clone() returns nil when Archivable = false, so g is nil and g:PivotTo fails. Fix: set Archivable = true on the template and its descendants (non-archivable descendants are silently left out of the clone), or set it to true just before cloning. Error 2: Destroy() sets Parent to nil and permanently locks the Parent property, disconnects the instance's connections and destroys its descendants. A destroyed instance cannot be reused. Correct pattern: keep one archivable template that never goes into the world (ServerStorage is best for server-only spawning). Clone it for every spawn, set the clone's pivot, parent the clone last, and Destroy the clone when the goblin dies. If you need pooling, park pooled clones (Parent = nil or a storage folder) instead of destroying them. Never destroy the template.
responses.R3:
Clone() returns nil when the instance's Archivable is false (Clone skips non-archivable instances and descendants), so template:Clone() is nil and :PivotTo errors. Fix: set Goblin.Archivable = true (or temporarily set it true before cloning and restore it).
Destroy() sets Parent to nil and locks the Parent property permanently (plus disconnects connections), so a destroyed instance can never be reparented: hence "Parent property ... is locked". Never Destroy a template you plan to reuse.
Correct pattern: keep the template in ServerStorage/ReplicatedStorage, Archivable = true, Clone() a fresh copy per spawn, PivotTo, parent to workspace, and Destroy() the clone (not the template) on death. If you need reuse for performance, pool clones and park them by setting Parent = nil or moving them away, not Destroy.

Destroy() sets Parent to nil and locks it permanently (also disconnects connections and marks it for cleanup), so the destroyed template can never be reparented: 'Parent property is locked'. Correct pattern: keep the template in ServerStorage (or ReplicatedStorage) with Archivable = true (set it back, or set template.Archivable = true in code before cloning), never parent or destroy the template, clone a fresh copy for each spawn, and Destroy() the clone when that goblin dies (or use a pool of clones that you reparent to nil/storage instead of destroying, if you want reuse).
responses.R5:
Error 1: Clone() skips instances whose Archivable is false. When the root itself is non-archivable, Clone() returns nil, so g:PivotTo fails with "attempt to index nil". Fix: set template.Archivable = true (fix or remove the plugin), or set it to true just before cloning.
Error 2: Destroy() sets Parent to nil and locks the Parent property permanently, and disconnects connections. A destroyed instance can never be reparented, so the 'reuse the template' plan breaks on the second spawn. It also destroys your only template.
Correct pattern: keep a never-parented, Archivable template in ServerStorage/ReplicatedStorage. Clone it for every spawn, and Destroy the clone when it dies (or Debris:AddItem it).
```lua
local template = game.ServerStorage.Enemies.Goblin
template.Archivable = true
local function spawnGoblin(cf)
  local g = template:Clone()
  g:PivotTo(cf)
  g.Parent = workspace
  g.Humanoid.Died:Once(function() task.delay(2, g.Destroy, g) end)
  return g
end
```
If you need reuse for performance, pool clones by parenting them to nil or to storage. Never Destroy a clone you plan to reuse.

Error 1: Instance:Clone() returns nil when the instance's Archivable is false. That is how the plugin's setting caused it: template:Clone() returned nil, then nil:PivotTo errors. Fix: set template.Archivable = true (and check descendants, since non-Archivable children are silently skipped in a clone). Add a guard: local g = template:Clone(); assert(g, "template not archivable").
Error 2: Destroy() sets Parent to nil and locks the Parent property permanently. It also disconnects connections and marks the instance for cleanup, so a destroyed instance can never be reparented. Destroy is final; never reuse a destroyed template.

When the goblin dies, Destroy the clone (e.g. Debris or a Humanoid.Died handler). To reuse instances (pooling), set Parent = nil (or move to a storage folder) instead of Destroy, then reset health and state before respawning.

prompt: Write a server-side melee hitbox in Luau: a 6x5x6 stud box centred 3 studs in front of the attacker's HumanoidRootPart; every other character inside takes 20 damage exactly once per swing; the attacker must be ignored. Use a spatial query rather than Touched, and note any accuracy caveat of the query you chose.
answer_key: workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox(cframe, size, overlapParams) with cframe = hrp.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 0, -3) (forward is -Z) and size Vector3.new(6, 5, 6)
OverlapParams that exclude the attacker's character: params.ExcludeInstances = {attackerChar}, or FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude with FilterDescendantsInstances = {attackerChar}
The query returns parts, so map each part to its character/Humanoid and keep a hit set so each Humanoid is damaged only once
GetPartBoundsInBox tests bounding boxes, not exact shapes (false positives on spheres, cylinders, meshes, unions); GetPartsInPart does a precise geometric check if accuracy matters

responses.R1:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local SIZE = Vector3.new(6, 5, 6)
local function swing(attacker: Model)
  local root = attacker:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
  if not root then return end
  local params = OverlapParams.new()
  params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {attacker}
  local cf = root.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 0, -3)
  local hit = {}
  for _, part in workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox(cf, SIZE, params) do
    local char = part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
    local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if hum and not hit[char] and hum.Health > 0 then
      hit[char] = true -- once per swing, not once per limb
      hum:TakeDamage(20)
    end
  end
end
```
Run this on the server when a validated swing request arrives, with a cooldown check. (The 2026 params.ExcludeInstances = {attacker} works too.) Caveat: GetPartBoundsInBox tests each part's axis-aligned bounding box, not its real geometry, so large or rotated parts and meshes can count as hits when they are only near the box. For exact overlap, use GetPartsInPart with a box part, at a higher cost. Lag also means the server sees positions slightly behind the client.

prompt: Write Luau that awards badge 123456789 when a player touches a finish-line part, done safely. List the conditions that must hold for the award to succeed.
answer_key: Call BadgeService:AwardBadgeAsync(player.UserId, badgeId) from a server Script (not a LocalScript), wrapped in pcall; it returns true when awarded
Guard against repeat calls: per-player debounce and/or check UserHasBadgeAsync first, and confirm the badge is enabled via GetBadgeInfoAsync(...).IsEnabled
Award only succeeds if the player is currently connected to the server, does not already own the badge, the badge is enabled, and it is awarded in a place belonging to the badge's experience

responses.R1:
```lua
local BadgeService = game:GetService("BadgeService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local BADGE_ID = 123456789
local awarded = {}
workspace.FinishLine.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
  local player = Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
  if not player or awarded[player] then return end
  awarded[player] = true
  local okHas, has = pcall(BadgeService.UserHasBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)
  if okHas and has then return end
  local ok, err = pcall(BadgeService.AwardBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)
  if not ok then awarded[player] = nil; warn(err) end -- allow retry
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) awarded[p] = nil end)
```

- The call runs in a server Script.
- The player is currently in this server.
- The player doesn't already own the badge.
- The badge is enabled (check with GetBadgeInfoAsync().IsEnabled).
- The badge belongs to this experience, and the place is part of it.
- You stay under the rate limit: 50 + 35 x players per minute, shared with UserHasBadgeAsync.
